players.product: AI servers and high-end computers: scaleX640 single-cabinet 640-card supernode, scaleX40 cable-free box supernode and scaleX supercluster; HPC systems; ParaStor / FlashNexus storage; immersion and cold-plate liquid cooling

quarterly_data.signal: H1 2026 results (half-year report): operating revenue RMB 7,465,810,151.43, up 27.62% from RMB 5,849,961,017.34; net profit attributable to shareholders RMB 971,389,448.14, up 33.31%; net profit excluding non-recurring items RMB 844,062,349.36, up 48.45%; operating cash flow -RMB 186,509,143.38 versus -RMB 1,381,335,558.12 a year earlier. Gross margin 27.23%, up 0.58 percentage points, which the company attributes to a higher share of high-end product sales improving the product mix. Investment income rose 40.58% to RMB 452,922,965.75, mainly from higher net profit at associates.

Company view (half-year report MD&A): compute demand grew explosively in the period, supernodes have become the mainstream form of AI compute infrastructure and domestic supernode products have entered a volume stage; with its supernode and supercluster product matrix positioned in the high-end supernode segment, plus continued compute-center construction, the company says it 'is expected to continue to benefit' from the industry's high growth. It says it achieved the leap in compute infrastructure from the ten-thousand-card class to the hundred-thousand-card class in H1 2026.

Supernode products (half-year report): in the period Sugon launched scaleX40, its first cable-free box-type supernode, integrating 40 GPUs in a single node with more than 28 PFLOPS (FP8) and more than 5TB of HBM, cutting compute-cluster deployment from months to hours; it forms a two-product matrix with the cabinet-level scaleX640 (launched 2025: 640 cards in a single cabinet, compute density up to 20 times higher, PUE as low as 1.04, supports multi-brand AI accelerator cards and scales to hundred-thousand-card clusters).
quarterly_data.figure: scaleX40: 40 GPUs, 28 PFLOPS (FP8), HBM over 5TB; scaleX640: 640 cards, PUE 1.04

quarterly_data.signal: Other new products (half-year report): a new-generation general-purpose HPC platform carrying the first domestic 10T-class general-purpose CPU (128 cores per processor, 10T FP64), with HPL double-precision relative performance up nearly 2 times and STREAM memory performance and average application performance each nearly doubled (up nearly 1 times) versus the previous generation; scaleFabric, the company's first self-developed 400G lossless high-speed network with native RDMA, for ten-thousand- and hundred-thousand-card clusters; FlashNexus 9000 centralized all-flash storage for AI training (200 million IOPS, 0.09ms latency). The company calls these four products a full-line first release.

Deployment (half-year report): in July 2026 the National Supercomputing Internet core node (Zhengzhou) went fully online; the company says the node is built on the Sugon scaleX supercluster as the country's first hundred-thousand-card-class converged supercomputing-intelligent compute pool, described in the report as the first fully domestic hundred-thousand-card supercluster.

Compute services (half-year report): by the end of H1 2026 the company's integrated compute network platform interconnected dozens of advanced computing centers, with more than 30 backbone-node compute centers; it aggregates more than 350 ten-thousand CPU cores and 25 ten-thousand GPU cards, has more than 140 ten-thousand registered users, more than 7300 application services and more than 1500 adapted large models.
quarterly_data.figure: over 30 backbone compute centers; 350 ten-thousand CPU cores; 25 ten-thousand GPU cards

quarterly_data.signal: Storage orders (half-year report): Sugon was shortlisted with the first share in China Mobile's centralized procurement of balanced distributed block storage, winning about RMB 1.8 hundred million, and won all five lots of China CRRC Group's storage product centralized procurement, covering distributed and centralized storage.
quarterly_data.figure: about RMB 1.8 hundred million (China Mobile); 5 of 5 lots (CRRC)

quarterly_data.signal: Liquid cooling (half-year report): subsidiary Sugon Shuchuang launched the C8000 V3.0 phase-change immersion liquid-cooling infrastructure, with single-cabinet power above 900kW, PUE below 1.04 and MW-class whole-cabinet delivery capability, under a 'liquid cooling as a service' model. The company says it has delivered 1650MW of data-center liquid-cooling systems and has ranked first in domestic liquid-cooling market share for five consecutive years (company claim).

R&D (half-year report): H1 2026 R&D investment RMB 10.94 hundred million, up 78.36%, equal to 14.65% of revenue (up 4.17 percentage points), supporting iteration of supernode and supercluster technology; R&D expense RMB 988,945,568.20, up 57.13%.
quarterly_data.figure: R&D RMB 10.94 hundred million (+78.36%), 14.65% of revenue

quarterly_data.signal: Orders and working capital (half-year report): inventory RMB 6,792,454,378.56 at end-June 2026 (15.72% of total assets), up 92.24% from year-end, which the company attributes mainly to more orders for high-end computers, converged compute-center projects and liquid-cooling projects; accounts payable rose 39.77% to RMB 6,302,678,004.41 on higher purchase volume; contract liabilities RMB 1,457,763,095.12 (+13.98%); construction in progress RMB 1,134,632,052.89 (+55.71%).

Development projects (half-year report): the company's three raised-fund R&D industrialization projects are an advanced compute cluster system for AI (next-generation supernode hardware, high-speed interconnect, system-level software stack and a heterogeneous compute management and operations platform, supporting hundred-thousand-card linear scaling with room for million-card scale), a next-generation high-performance AI training-and-inference appliance based on domestic CPUs and AI accelerator cards, and a domestic advanced storage system (all-flash arrays and other core components); they map to its compute-cluster, AI-server and storage product lines.

Related-party trade (half-year report): for 2026 the company expects sales of products and services of RMB 500,000.00 ten-thousand to associate Z (RMB 207,354.48 ten-thousand contracted and executed from the start of 2026 to the disclosure date), RMB 114,544.00 ten-thousand to associate Y (31,745.95 executed) and RMB 10,000.00 ten-thousand to associate X (3,173.93 executed); expected purchases are RMB 20,000.00 ten-thousand from Z, 40,000.00 from Y and 20,000.00 from X. The associates' names are not disclosed.
quarterly_data.figure: associate Z sales: RMB 207,354.48 ten-thousand executed of RMB 500,000.00 ten-thousand expected for 2026

quarterly_data.signal: Major construction-in-progress projects at end-June 2026 (half-year report, self-funded): Tianjin No. 16 renovation and expansion (budget RMB 370,000,000.00, 98.33% complete), Yinshang cloud data center (budget RMB 167,000,000.00, 87.50%), Zhengzhou advanced computing institute data center building (budget RMB 307,831,700.00, 55.15%) and research building (budget RMB 602,681,600.00, 21.36%), Taiyuan industrial base (budget RMB 204,002,600.00, 56.48%), Anhui science and innovation center (budget RMB 347,000,000.00, 37.72%), Jinan base (budget RMB 330,000,000.00, 9.56%) and Shanghai AI industrialization base (budget RMB 148,500,000.00, 1.47%). No completion dates are stated.

Supply chain (half-year report risk section): the company says it still needs foreign advanced components in frontier areas and that, since the further US Commerce Department Entity List restriction of October 2022, its purchases of foreign advanced components have been affected; it is adapting products with domestic suppliers and says slower progress there could hurt it.

Sugon.why: Chinese high-end computer and AI server maker (scaleX640 / scaleX40 supernodes, scaleX supercluster) sold with multi-brand AI accelerator cards and domestic CPUs; its stock rises with AI server and data-center CPU platform demand.
Sugon.evidence: Sugon half-year report: 2026 Half-Year Report (08-26-2026): high-end computers are the core business; launched scaleX40 (40 GPUs per node) alongside the 640-card scaleX640; inventory up 92.24% on more high-end computer orders.
